  • typedef HxResult(*) HxWidgetDrawFnPtr (HxWidget_t *pWidget, HxRegion_t *pRegion, bool clear)
    The widget Draw callback function is called when the system event queue is idle, and if the bounds of the widget is within the update region. The update region is accumulated by the OS as visible widgets are created or as they change state, and by explicit calls to HxWidgetUpdate. The third parameter determines whether the region should be cleared first before drawing.
  • typedef HxResult(*) HxWidgetDestroyFnPtr (HxWidget_t *pWidget)
    The widget Destroy callback function should deallocate any objects explicitly allocated when the widget was created. The application should always call the toolkit's default Destroy callback before returning so that the toolkit has an opportunity to delete any toolkit objects that may have been allocated.
  • typedef HxResult(*) HxWidgetSetFocusFnPtr (HxWidget_t *pWidget, bool focus)

  • typedef HxResult(*) HxWidgetSetEnabledFnPtr (HxWidget_t *pWidget, bool enabled)
    The widget SetEnabled callback function is called when a widget's focus is either disabled (enabled == false) or enabled (enabled == true). A disabled widget does not receive input events, and is typically drawn "grayed out".
  • typedef HxResult(*) HxWidgetSetVisibleFnPtr (HxWidget_t *pWidget, bool visible)

  • typedef HxResult(*) HxWidgetDirectFocusFnPtr (HxWidget_t **hWidget, HxFocusDirection_t direction)
    The DirectFocus callback is used by the HTML widget so that it can control focus-handling, and bypass the default system focus-handling. hWidget is an IN/OUT argument, that may be changed by the callback to a different widget, or NULL if no widget has focus.

#define HxWidgetGetFocusRingWidth (  )     2

Return the focus ring width.

HxWidgetGetFocusRingWidth returns the width of the typical focus ring. The value returned is not accurate for command buttons, which have a focus width of 4 pixels.

The focus ring is drawn outside the client area of the widget, so the application should take this width into consideration when laying out widgets.

To ensure more accurate layout coordinates, applications can compare the bounds returned from HxWidgetGetBounds (bounds of the widget including the focus ring and frame) with the bounds returned from HxWidgetGetClientBounds (bounds not including the focus ring and frame). Use HxFieldAdviseHeight for fields and HxListBoxAdviseHeightWidth for list boxes.

typedef int32_t(*) HxWidgetOnButtonDownFnPtr(HxWidget_t *pWidget, int32_t x, int32_t y, HxMouseButton_t button)

The OnButtonDown callback function is called when the button down occurs within the bounds of the widget.

Applications cannot override the OnButtonDown callback for certain compound widgets (HxFileList_t and HxStorageList_t), because the event is passed to underlying components.

If the application implements a button down callback for an HxContainer_t, use the kHxContainerAttrKeepEvents flag to avoid having the motion event passed to the container's children.

In general, applications should use HxListenToMessage, defined in hxmessage.h, to listen for the button "action" message. Alternatively, to target a specific widget rather than all widgets of a particular type, use HxWidgetMapMessageCallback. For example, listen for kHxCommandButtonChanged for command button selection, kHxCheckboxChanged for a checkbox toggle, or kHxGadgetSelected for a button down and up within a gadget.

HxResult HxWidgetAllocateID ( uint32_t *  pID  ) 

Allocate a new widget ID.

HxWidgetAllocateID returns a unique dynamically-allocated ID, which can then be used to create a new widget. Normally, apps should just pass in kHxWidgetAutoID to a widget create function to get an auto-generated ID. Currently the only way to unallocate an ID is to create and then destroy a widget that uses the ID.

Parameters:
pID OUT: New ID
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_FAILURE if a new ID cannot be allocated.

HxResult HxWidgetDrawFocusRing ( HxWidget_t *  pWidget,
bool  hasFocus 
)

Draw the focus ring for a widget.

HxWidgetDrawFocusRing is provided for applications that wish to have control over when and where focus rings are drawn.

Normally, applications should allow the system to take care of drawing the focus ring. But this function can be used if, for example, the application has a non-focusable container containing a field with no frame: the application can use HxWidgetDrawFocusRing to draw a focus ring around the container when the field gains focus, and erase the ring when the field loses focus.

This function cannot be called on a HxWindow_t*.

This function calls the widget's Draw callback.

Parameters:

Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxWidgetFindChild returns the widget located at the window coordinates (*pX, *pY). pX and pY are returned with child-relative coordinates.

HxResult HxWidgetGetClientBounds ( HxWidget_t *  pWidget,
HxRectangle_t *  pBounds 
)

Return the bounds of a widget's client area.

HxWidgetGetClientBounds is an accessor for the bounds of the client area of a widget. This bound is relative to it's non-client area, so you will see small values for x and y, or 0 for both if there is no border around the widget. The system uses the non-client area to draw the widget's focus ring and/or frame. You can use this API along with HxWidgetGetBounds to determine just how off-center the client area is within the widget.

pBounds must point to an HxRectangle_t structure.

For windows, this acts similar to HxWidgetGetBounds, returning the area of the window via a call to HxWindowGetBounds. For dialogs, the origin will have small values that represent the dialog frames, which are not part of the window's client area.

Parameters:
pWidget IN: Pointer to widget
pBounds OUT: Pointer to the bounds of a widget
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxWidgetGetFocusedWidget ( HxWidget_t **  hWidget  ) 

Get the focused widget[s].

The OS maintains the focus order of widgets, which is used for keyboard navigation. When the main application window is active, the set of focusable widgets include the focusable widgets in the main application window as well as the widgets in the application bar. When a dialog is open, the set of focusable widgets only include the focusable widgets in the dialog.

HxResult HxWidgetMapMessageCallback ( HxWidget_t *  pWidget,
int32_t  messageClass,
int32_t  messageAction,
HxMessageCallback  pCallback,
void *  pData 
)

A message callbacks is the normal way an application reacts to user actions. This is the recommended way to respond to events, rather than using the HxWidgetSetCallback API, which replaces the low-level event handler.

This function associates a message callback with a particular message action, such as a command button press or a double click in a list.

If pWidget is NULL, then the callback is called for any message sender. If pWidget is not NULL, the callback is only called when that widget is the sender of the message.

messageClass would be set to kHxActionMessageClass for messages associated with widgets, or set to kHxInputMessageClass for input messages from the keyboard, mouse, or scroll wheel.

messageAction would be set to the type of message for which the application is listening (i.e., kHxCheckboxChanged). See messagedomain.h for a full listing.

An application can associate more than one messageAction and callback with a widget. Messages associated with a widget will be unregistered by the system when the widget is destroyed.

If pCallback is NULL, the callback for the message action associated with the widget is removed. Note that this should not be done for broadcasted messages.

HX_INVALID_ARG is returned if pWidget is a pointer to a HxWindow_t. If an application wants to listen to input events for a window, use HxWindowSetHandler (see hxwindow.h) or HxMessageListen (see hxmessage.h).

Parameters:
pWidget IN: Pointer to a widget
messageClass IN: Message class (kHxActionMessageClass or kHxInputMessageClass)
messageAction IN: Type of message
pCallback IN: Callback function, or NULL
pData IN: Pointer to user data, or NULL
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_INVALID_ARG if messageAction is not valid.

HxResult HxWidgetSetCallback ( HxWidget_t *  pWidget,
HxCallbackSelector_t  selector,
void *  pCallback,
void **  hOldCallback 
)

Set (and get) a widget's callback.

Widget callbacks are called by the system in response to events. For example, command buttons have callbacks for button down, button up, and key down events. This function makes it possible for the application to override a widget's callbacks.

pCallback can be set to NULL if the caller only wants hOldCallback returned.

If hOldCallback is not NULL, the old callback is returned. Normally, an application should call the default system callback after performing its custom operation. For example, the application can use this function to save the default Draw callback, calling it after performing any custom drawing in its widget.

Normally, a pointer to an HxWindow_t structure should never be passed to an HxWidget API. It is appropriate, however, for applications to override the certain callbacks. HX_INVALID_ARG is returned, however, if a window is passed to this function for the following widget-specific callbacks:

kHxWidgetFocusStateChange kHxWidgetEnabledStateChange kHxWidgetVisibleStateChange kHxWidgetResize kHxWidgetDirectFocus

Parameters:
pWidget IN: Pointer to the widget
selector IN: Callback selector
pCallback IN: Pointer to a widget's callback, or NULL
hCallback OUT: Handle to a widget's old callback, or NULL
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success.

HxResult HxWidgetSetFocus ( HxWidget_t *  pWidget  ) 

Moves focus to a specific widget.

HxWidgetSetFocus causes a widget to gain or lose focus.

By default, when the application calls HxWindowEventLoop, the first widget allocated is given focus. When a widget loses focus, the OS gives focus to the next focusable widget in the focus array (see HxWidgetSetFocusArray). The application can override this behavior with this function.

If the widget is not focusable, HX_OK is returned, and an error message is sent to stderr on debug builds.

If you want to remove focus from all widgets, you can pass NULL as pWidget. This will unfocus everything; the next focus move operation will go to the first focusable item in the active focus array.

Parameters:
pWidget IN: Pointer to widget or NULL to clear focus
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxWidgetSetFocusArray ( const uint32_t *  pIdArray,
int32_t  idCount 
)

Change the widget focus order.

By default, the focus order of widgets is by order of creation.

HxWidgetSetFocusArray allows the application to change the focus order of the widgets contained within a window. This function should be called before calling HxWindowEventLoop.

The ID array should normally contain all of the widget ID's in the window. If an invalid ID is passed into the array, no error is returned, but any missing widgets will no longer be capable of receiving focus for purposes of keyboard navigation.

Passing an idCount of 0 disables the toolkit's handling of keyboard navigation for the topmost visible window. If idCount is 0, then pIdArray can be NULL. Use HxWindowSetFocusArray to clear the focus array for a window other than the topmost visible window.

If widgets are allocated after this function is called, the new widgets are appended to the focus array.

Parameters:
pIdArray IN: Array of widget ID's
idCount IN: Size of the widget ID array
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxWidgetSetFrameType ( HxWidget_t *  pWidget,
HxWidgetFrame_t  frame,
HxWidgetFrame_t *  pOldFrame 
)

Override focus ring drawing.

HxWidgetSetFrameType is provided to applications that wish to override the system focus ring behavior. It allows an application to draw a focus ring on a widget that does not have focus, such as a focusable container that encloses an unframed field.

Only limited support is offered. The frame argument can be set to kHxFrameOnly, which draws the frame used by lists, fields, and gadgets. Or the frame argument can be set to kHxFrameWithFocusRing, which draws this frame with a focus ring.

If pWidget is a widget that does not use the standard frame type, then HX_INVALID_ARG is returned, and the frame is left unchanged.

HX_INVALID_ARG is returned if the frame argument is invalid. If pOldFrame is not NULL, the old frame type is returned.

Parameters:
pID IN: Pointer to widget
frame IN: Frame type
pOldFrame OUT: Pointer to old frame, or NULL
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_INVALID_ARG if invalid selector passed in frame.

Set input receiver.

HxWidgetSetInputReceiver specifies a widget that should receive mouse and keyboard events. If the widget does not handle input events, HX_OK is returned, and an error message is sent to stderr on debug builds.

This function can be used to override the system behavior when the widget focus changes. By default, when the widget focus changes, the widget that gains focus also becomes the input receiver.

HxWidgetUpdate passes a region within the bounds of the widget to define as a dirty region that needs an update. Note that this does not cause the widget to be drawn until the next update action.
